title: Alkaline-phosphatase–phosphate coupling did not establish incremental hip-density prediction across separate NHANES samples
abstract: A literature-motivated mineralization-stress interaction was tested using existing public data, not new experiments. We trained fixed weighted ridge spline models in 1,550 NHANES 2005–2006 adults aged 50+ and transported them to 2,280 separately sampled 2007–2008 adults. Adding centered log alkaline phosphatase × centered log phosphorus to separate chemistry and conventional covariates changed total-femur BMD prediction MSE from 0.01430512 to 0.01429703. The difference was -0.00000809 (two-sample stratified PSU-bootstrap 95% interval -0.00004669 to 0.00007699); source grouped cross-validation worsened. The registered benefit criterion failed. This is a scoped negative representational test, not a diagnosis of osteomalacia or evidence against biochemical bone physiology. Author source auditing corrected source creatinine calibration and clean reruns reproduced the final outputs. Complete-case selection, total rather than bone-specific enzyme measurement, missing medication/vitamin-D adjustment and shared survey methods limit generalization.
